name: Familial Isolated Pituitary Adenoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Familial Isolated Pituitary Adenoma Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of two or more first-degree relatives with pituitary adenomas without other syndromic features
Radiological or histopathological confirmation of pituitary adenoma in affected family members
Exclusion of other familial syndromes associated with pituitary adenomas such as MEN1 or Carney complex
Identification of germline mutations in AIP gene or other associated genes (supportive)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: At least two first-degree relatives with confirmed pituitary adenomas and exclusion of other syndromic causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for AIP mutations can support diagnosis but is not mandatory.

pathognomonic.notes: Commonly presents with headache and visual field defects

pathognomonic.symptomName: Hypersecretion of pituitary hormones (e.g., prolactin, growth hormone)
searchTerms: overproduction of prolactin or growth hormone

common.symptomName: Bitemporal hemianopsia due to optic chiasm compression
searchTerms: loss of side vision in both eyes
tunnel vision from optic chiasm pressure

common.symptomName: Acromegalic features from growth hormone excess
searchTerms: acromegaly signs from growth hormone excess
headache not related to tumor size

rare.symptomName: Cranial nerve palsies due to cavernous sinus invasion
searchTerms: cranial nerve weakness from tumor spread
nerve palsies due to cavernous sinus invasion

rare.symptomName: Pituitary apoplexy presenting with sudden headache and visual loss

laboratory: Elevated serum prolactin, growth hormone, or other pituitary hormone levels depending on adenoma subtype
Low levels of pituitary target hormones in hypopituitarism
imaging: MRI showing pituitary adenoma with or without suprasellar extension
Compression of optic chiasm on imaging
other: Histopathological confirmation of adenoma subtype after surgery

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of parathyroid and pancreatic tumors
Cardiac myxomas and skin pigmentation abnormalities
Multiple endocrine tumors including pituitary but with additional systemic features

redFlags: Rapid onset of visual field defects
Signs of pituitary apoplexy (sudden headache, vomiting, altered consciousness)
Severe hypopituitarism symptoms such as adrenal crisis
references: Beckers A, et al. Familial Isolated Pituitary Adenomas: Clinical and Genetic Aspects. Endocr Rev. 2013;34(2):239-277.
Chahal HS, et al. AIP mutations and familial isolated pituitary adenomas. Endocrine-Related Cancer. 2011;18(6):R185-R195.
